chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A man came to Ali (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'There is a debt of mine upon a man, so he gave me a gift.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Count it from your debt upon him.'
ai.seo_question: How is a gift from a debtor treated in relation to an outstanding debt according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on gifting by creditors, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal presumption that a gift from a debtor to a creditor is intended as debt repayment unless explicitly stated otherwise. This ruling reflects the practical Shia jurisprudence of *istishab* (presumption of continuity), ensuring that financial transactions are interpreted in light of the debtor's likely intent to settle obligations. It underscores the importance of clarity in financial dealings while favoring the resolution of debts through such gestures.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There is a debt for me upon a man, so he gifted a gift to me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Count it from your debt upon him (as a part repayment of debt)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

once a man came to Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said, ‘Someone who owes to me a certain amount of debts has sent me a gift.’ He (the Imam) Alayhi al- Salam, said, ‘Count it as part of payment for what he owes you.’”
